files.Title: Playcraft.Core.AgeFit
files.Summary: One age band's suitability envelope for a catalog part: whether the part is appropriate for the band and, for elevated parts, the deck-height range it physically fits. min = max = 0 is the file's convention for ground-mounted and height-independent parts: ground level only once the structure's band is known, any height while it is not (see ).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.AuditAgeBand
files.Summary: The age band a limit is read at. The design team's rules are written per band and the two numbers differ by a factor of 1.5 or more, so which band applies is never a detail.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.AuditComponent
files.Summary: One placed component as the audit sees it — the neutral shape the Plugin harvests from ComponentScan so the rules stay AutoCAD-free (invariant 8).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.AuditFinding
files.Summary: One thing the audit found.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.AuditLimit
files.Summary: One rule's limit in inches, per age band, with the wiki card it came from.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.AuditMate
files.Summary: One of a component's mate points, with what already sits on it.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.AuditReport
files.Summary: What one audit pass produced: the findings, and an honest account of what could not be checked.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.AuditRuleBook
files.Summary: The design team's rulebook as data: the numeric limits, the part classification the limits are applied to, and the limb-climber catalog table. Read from data/audit/ (invariant 10's sidecar rule — the numbers are versioned with the code, never scattered as literals through src/), and every entry carries the wiki card it was transcribed from so a printed finding cites its source.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.BomCalculator
files.Summary: Pure BOM math. Descriptions come from the catalog cache when present, falling back to built-in labels for unenriched parts — never the network. Lives in Core so the tallying rules are unit-testable without AutoCAD; the Cad layer's only job is collecting s from the drawing.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.BomCsv
files.Summary: Composes the priced, sectioned, per-level BOM as CSV text — the office file for sales, purchasing and the factory (execution plan Item 3). Pure text composition so the layout is unit-testable; the Cad layer owns the file write and its encoding (UTF-8 with BOM, so Excel detects it).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.BomCsvResult
files.Summary: What produced: the file text plus the counts of what it actually rendered, so the command's report can describe the FILE rather than the flat tally it was built from (the same part at the same level in two structures is one flat row but two data rows here).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.BomLine
files.Summary: A bill-of-materials line: one distinct part with its quantity.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.BomLineRules
files.Summary: Which rule produced a bill-of-materials line, named with the reference build it follows - so a count the order desk disputes can be explained. Derived from the line's part number and description against the constants; every other line is a placed component.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.BomSection
files.Summary: One section of a sectioned BOM: a play structure or a freestanding bucket, with the lines belonging to it. A quote prints these in order so no component is orphaned from the structure it belongs to.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.Box3
files.Summary: An axis-aligned 3D box in drawing inches. Deliberately free of AutoCAD and WPF types.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.BoxGrid
files.Summary: A uniform 2D hash grid over indexed boxes (bucketed by XY footprint; Z is checked in the exact intersection test). Same contract as : the grid narrows candidates, and every match re-runs the exact predicate — including its closed-interval touching-faces semantics — so results match a full O(n²) scan bit-for-bit.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.CatalogFilter
files.Summary: Catalog compatibility rules, straight from the catalog file's own data: which parts fit a clicked host (MatesWith family + system type + the age envelopes' deck-height range) and which suit an age band.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.CatalogFit
files.Summary: A "show me what fits this" context: the placed component a designer clicked, reduced to the three facts compatibility depends on.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.CatalogLookup
files.Summary: One lookup response: cacheable parts, volatile prices, and misses.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.CatalogPart
files.Summary: Catalog metadata for one part as returned by the catalog service — everything EXCEPT price. Price is volatile and is deliberately never cached into drawings; these fields are stable identity data that make a drawing self-describing offline.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.CatalogPayload
files.Summary: Parses catalog lookup responses into values, tolerating shape quirks in the feed.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.CatalogQuery
files.Summary: A designer's search box text, parsed: the terms an entry must match and the terms that disqualify it. A term may be a bare word or a quoted phrase; the distinction is gone by the time it lands here, because both are matched the same way (as a contiguous substring).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.CatalogSearch
files.Summary:
The catalog search: how a designer's typing turns into a ranked list.

Three things the plain substring filter it replaces could not do. It ranks, so typing "deck" puts the square deck above the hundred parts whose DESCRIPTION happens to say "deck". It ignores punctuation in part numbers, so S-1101-R5, s1101r5 and 1101 all find the same deck. And when a query matches nothing at all it retries with a bounded edit distance, so one fat-fingered letter returns the part instead of an empty list — but only then, and it says so, because a fuzzy match that quietly displaces exact ones is worse than no match.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.CatalogSearchResult
files.Summary: What a search found: the entries in relevance order, plus the near-miss term when nothing matched exactly and the search fell back to spelling tolerance. is non-null only in that case, so the palette can say the results are approximate instead of pretending.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.CatalogSort
files.Summary: Sorting for the catalog palette. One rule is worth stating out loud: a part with no price sorts LAST whichever direction the price column is pointing. Ascending, an unpriced part is not "cheapest"; descending, it is not "most expensive". Missing data is missing data, and letting it win either end of the list is how a designer picks a part believing something the catalog never said.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.CatalogSortKey
files.Summary: The column a designer sorted the catalog by.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.CollarBoxes
files.Summary: The collar model from a part's 3D drawing: one box per entity on a collar layer, in the 3D model's own frame, so the collar placement and counting that read the XAML models read the drawings unchanged.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.CollarCounter
files.Summary: Collar counting. A collar is a physical clamp on a post; the component library models them as named meshes in each component's 3D art, so the count is derived from mesh bounding boxes: where two components share a post their collar boxes coincide and merge into one physical collar.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.CollarModel
files.Summary: The collar meshes of one part's 3D model, by kind, in the model's own coordinates (X/Z horizontal plane, Y up).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.CollarPlacement
files.Summary: Where a placed part's collars stand in the drawing — the half of the collar rule that comes before . The counter merges boxes that overlap; this decides where each part's boxes are, and a count is only as right as that.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.CollarSources
files.Summary: Where a part's collars come from once the drawings are the library.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.ComponentLibrary
files.Summary: The component catalog parsed from the library's ComponentData.xml: every entry, plus the library's own rule for which families are browsable. The file marks auto-inserted families (posts, fillers, caps) as omitted from the library tree; the browsable view honors that so designers see exactly the parts they are meant to place by hand.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.ComponentTypes
files.Summary: The component TYPE tags written into each placed component's identity tag. Domain vocabulary shared by the Cad layer (which stores them as XData) and the BOM math here — the strings themselves are drawing data, so they must never change once drawings exist.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DeckHeightCheck
files.Summary: The verdict on a requested deck height, with the part's rated bounds so a refusal message can say what WOULD be accepted.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DeckHeightRule
files.Summary: The deck-height editing rule shared by every entry point that accepts a height (PBHEIGHT, PBSTAMP's prompt, the KCD importer's warning): heights live on the catalog's 6" grid, inside the 6" to 156" editing range, under the 108" cap for surface-mount decks, and inside the part's own age envelopes. A height that breaks a rule is refused with a named reason, never silently rewritten. The envelope semantic is 's: the structure's own age band when its design file names one, any appropriate band when it does not, and missing data never blocks, so the editing rule and the catalog fit filter can never disagree.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DeckHeightVerdict
files.Summary: Which rule refused a requested deck height, or .

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DeckJointPart
files.Summary: A placed part as the joint-hardware rules see it: deck-to-deck () and erector-rock ().

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DeckToDeck
files.Summary: Which decks are physically attached: the adjacency behind structure membership (). This is NOT the deck-to-deck hardware count, which joins only decks of one height at their mate points (); two decks at different heights sharing an edge are one structure but take no deck-to-deck set.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DeckToDeckCounts
files.Summary: How many deck-to-deck hardware sets a structure needs.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DeckToDeckHardware
files.Summary: The deck-to-deck hardware rule of the reference implementation: one set for every place where two decks of the same height meet at a mate point.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DependencyBinding
files.Summary: One resolved owner→dependent pairing in a design: which placed slide carries which placed sit-down wall/hood (or, generally, which owner carries which dependent), and how the two are linked.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DependencyCatalog
files.Summary: The owner→dependent auto-carry rule table, built from the component catalog's own declarations. An OWNER (a slide, a climber) names the dependent Categories it carries; a DEPENDENT (a sit-down wall/hood, a half/transition wall) carries the matching . This catalog resolves a placed component — keyed the way a design file names it, FileName then PartNumber — to those facts so can pair owners with the dependents they auto-carry.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DependencyFinding
files.Summary: One thing wrong with a design's dependency graph.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DependencyIssue
files.Summary: The kind of dependency issue reports.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DependencyPlan
files.Summary: The complete dependency picture for a design: every resolved owner→dependent binding, plus every issue (missing, broken, orphaned, inconsistent). A command reconciles a drawing against it, and a MOVE/DELETE of an owner reads to carry its dependents.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DependencyPlanner
files.Summary: The dependency pass over a whole design: pairs every owner (slide, climber) with the dependents it auto-carries (sit-down wall/hood, half/transition wall) and reports the graph's gaps. Pure and vault-independent — the drawing analogue of , but driven by the design file's own attachment links rather than deck geometry.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DependencyTally
files.Summary: The headline numbers of a , counted once so a reporting command never has to derive them (and never double-counts a single drifted pair, which both emitters would otherwise invite: Pass 1 anchors the finding on the dependent, Pass 2 on the owner, but each still describes exactly one binding).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DependentChoice
files.Summary: The catalog parts an owner could carry, and whether the choice is the designer's to make. Placement asks this before it asks the designer: a slide whose sit-down wall is determined needs no prompt, a climber with four themed half walls does.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DependentPairing
files.Summary: Item 15, "pairing comes from positions too": which owner (a slide, a climber) a dependent (a sit-down wall, a half wall) belongs to, decided by where the two sit, so a wall placed by hand pairs exactly as one the plugin placed.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DependentSelector
files.Summary: Which catalog parts satisfy an owner's for a given structure. The rule table () says WHAT categories an owner carries; this says WHICH parts can fill them here, which is what a placement command needs before it can carry anything.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignAudit
files.Summary: The design team's geometry rules as predicates (execution plan Item 10). Report only, forever by default: nothing here moves, refuses or repairs anything. The rule is the designer's to overrule.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignAuditRecord
files.Summary: A review record: who reviewed which content, when.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignBomLine
files.Summary: One bill-of-materials line with the rule that produced it.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignCompliance
files.Summary: A structure's compliance values.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignDocument
files.Summary: The suite's own record of a design (Item 22): what the drawing holds, structure by structure, with every bill-of-materials line and the rule that made it, compliance values with their provenance, prices with their source, review records keyed on a content hash, and the link to the legacy design file written beside it. The legacy file is a projection of this document. Serialized by , read back by , validated by .

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignDocumentBuilder
files.Summary: Builds the design document an export writes: parts in the drawing's world frame with position-based keys, every bill-of-materials line with its rule, the counts the legacy tab records, compliance values with their rules, prices per structure, and audit records carried forward.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignDocumentReader
files.Summary: Reads a back from JSON, strictly: the text is validated against first, and anything the schema refuses is refused here with the failing path named. Also projects a document onto the legacy model (), so every command that reads a legacy design file can read a document instead.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignDocumentSchema
files.Summary: The design document's JSON Schema (2020-12), embedded in this assembly from data/schema/design.schema.json so every caller validates against the same file with nothing to configure.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignDocumentWriter
files.Summary: Writes a as JSON: camelCase, indented with two spaces and line feeds, every field in a fixed order, real numbers and booleans, null for unknown. The same document always serializes to the same bytes on every platform.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignEnvelope
files.Summary: The document's envelope.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignExportInput
files.Summary: Everything one export hands to .

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignExportStructure
files.Summary: One structure as an export hands it to : the legacy tab it wrote (re-read from the written file) plus what only the drawing knows about it.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignExtraHardware
files.Summary: The extra-hardware band decision for one play structure.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignFrame
files.Summary: The legacy canvas frame: canvas = (x + shift.x, -(y + shift.y)) for a world position (x, y). The shift is zero for a design imported from a legacy file (import places parts at the file's own coordinates, Y-flipped) and the canvas-centering translation for a design the New export authored.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignHardwareCounts
files.Summary: The hardware counts a structure's legacy tab records; null where it records none.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignHashes
files.Summary: The document's content hashes. Formatting of the JSON never affects one.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignKeys
files.Summary: Part identity across tools: position and name, never a GUID a reader may renew. The same rendering the legacy writer's content comparison uses, so a change the writer counts is a change the document's hash counts.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignLegacy
files.Summary: The link to the legacy design file.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignLegacyTab
files.Summary: One structure's legacy tab.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignPart
files.Summary: One part of a structure.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignPricedStructure
files.Summary: One structure's prices.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignPricing
files.Summary: The document's prices.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignRuledValue
files.Summary: A value with the rule it came from; a null value is honestly unknown.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignSchemaError
files.Summary: One way a document fails its schema.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignSchemaResult
files.Summary: What validating a document against its schema found.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignSettings
files.Summary: What a structure declares about itself.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignStructure
files.Summary: One structure: a designer's named group, written as one legacy design tab.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DesignUnassigned
files.Summary: A component the export could see and did not write.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DwgMarker
files.Summary: One insert a part drawing holds, in the drawing's model-space frame (inches).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DwgMarkerKind
files.Summary: What a marker insert in a part's 2D drawing stands for.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DwgPolyline
files.Summary: One polyline run a part drawing holds (lines, arcs and circles arrive as runs too), model space.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.DwgSolidBox
files.Summary: The bounds of one entity of a part's 3D drawing, in the drawing's own frame (Z up).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.ElevationDrift
files.Summary: Whether an edit that moved a part in Z left the drawing disagreeing with itself — the rule behind the OSNAPZ trap.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.ElevationDriftKind
files.Summary: What an edit did to a part's elevation, judged against where the part stood before it.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.EnvFile
files.Summary: Line-level editing for the suite's per-user settings files: plain text, one KEY="value" per line, # comments. Editing works on lines rather than a parsed model on purpose — a settings file may hold keys and comments this code has never heard of, and a save must let them all through untouched.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.ErectorRockHardware
files.Summary: The erector-rock hardware rule of the reference implementation: one set of for every pair of erector rocks joined end to end.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.ExistingPost
files.Summary: A post already in the drawing, as the reconciler sees it.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.ExtraHardware
files.Summary: The extra-hardware allowance (HS-1007): a priced number of spare-hardware sets per play structure, banded on what the structure costs.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.ExtraHardwareBand
files.Summary: What the band rule decided for one structure.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.ExtraHardwareBasis
files.Summary: Which price column the extra-hardware rule bands a structure on.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.FallHeightAndCapacity
files.Summary: A structure's maximum fall height and child capacity, with the parts that had no catalog facts to contribute (both values may then be low).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.FallHeightRule
files.Summary: The maximum fall height and child capacity of one structure, from its parts' catalog facts. A part's fall height is its catalog fall height plus its adjustment; when the catalog gives the fall height as "AUTO" it is the part's placed design height plus the adjustment instead. The structure's maximum is the largest of its parts' and never below 0. Its child capacity is each part's capacity times the copies the placement stands for, summed. Fall height stays a fact of its own: only an "AUTO" part derives it from the placed height, and nothing writes it back into the instance height.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.FeatureCatalog
files.Summary: Strict loader for data/features.json. Anything the schema forbids — missing fields, malformed command names, duplicate commands — throws rather than degrading silently, because two consumers (palette and docs) would otherwise drift apart in different ways.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.FeatureDefinition
files.Summary: One user-facing plugin feature as declared in data/features.json — the single source of truth consumed by BOTH the AutoCAD palette and the documentation site's End-User tab. Mirrors data/features.schema.json.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.FillerAction
files.Summary: What to do about the filler at one shared mate point.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.FillerCatalog
files.Summary: The filler catalog parsed from the library's FillerData.xml: the per-system dimension tables the selection rule searches, the swap groups behind the "swap filler" UI, and the global 6-inch-gap flag.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.FillerDecision
files.Summary: The resolved filler action for one shared mate point.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.FillerDeck
files.Summary: One deck-like component as the filler pass sees it, all geometry in world drawing coordinates (Y up, inches).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.FillerEntry
files.Summary: One filler part's dimension entry from the library's FillerData.xml.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.FillerMatePoint
files.Summary: A deck mate point in world drawing coordinates.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.FillerPlacement
files.Summary: One filler the plan wants standing in the drawing.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.FillerPlan
files.Summary: The complete filler plan for a drawing: where fillers belong and where any existing filler must go away (flush joints and suppressed 6" steps).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.FillerPlanner
files.Summary: The filler pass over a whole drawing: pairs the deck-like components the legacy way (shared posts + coincident mate points) and folds the per-point decisions of into one position-keyed plan a command can reconcile the drawing against.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.FillerSelector
files.Summary: Filler auto-selection: the legacy engine's exact lookup and trigger rules, ported as pure functions (see docs/pd-parity.md). A filler is a vertical spacer bridging the height step where two mated decks of different DesignHeights meet on shared posts — one per shared mate point per height-differing deck pair. It is NOT emitted on open perimeter edges. The legacy trigger pairs decks hanging off a common post that share at least two posts and coincident mate points, then decides per shared mate point as does.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.FootprintStackRule
files.Summary: The stacking half of the magnet: a deck clicked ON another deck's footprint is born at that deck's exact plan position instead of at the raw pick, so a tower can be dragged instead of typed.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.FreestandingSections
files.Summary: Quote sections for components a designer left outside every group. The bucket names come from the component library's own family vocabulary, which the bundled price list repeats verbatim, so they resolve with no vault and no network.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.HardwareCalculator
files.Summary: Builds the counted-hardware BOM lines from design tallies.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.HardwareRules
files.Summary: Counted-hardware rules: the BOM lines that are tallies of the design rather than placed components — collars, post caps, deck-to-deck and erector-rock hardware, and the price-banded extra-hardware allowance. Part numbers and system-type mappings are ports of the legacy BOM output rules, verified against the current price list.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.HeightLabel
files.Summary: The height attribute's value format — the one string that is BOTH the designer-visible label and the canonical stored height (ADR §4.4a: the attribute owns height, there is no second copy). Because storage and display are the same string, must round-trip every height the suite handles: "0.####" keeps a hand-edited 40.25" exact where the old display-only "0.#" would have stored it back as 40.3".

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.HeightResolver
files.Summary: Height resolution for placement flows (F-032): what height metadata a placement should carry, and whether a part is rated for the host height it snapped to. Pure functions over catalog data, shared by the magnetic placement jig and the catalog fit filter so the two can never disagree about what "fits at this height" means.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.HeightStamp
files.Summary: The height a placement is stamped with, and how the part's own age band shaped it.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.HeightStampKind
files.Summary: How the placed part's own age band shaped the height it is stamped with.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdAttachmentPoint
files.Summary: One attachment point of a component in a legacy design file. In the file these are FLAT repeatable <AttachmentPoints> elements with the fields as direct children — there is no per-point wrapper element.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdComponent
files.Summary: One placed component in a legacy design file.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdComponentAddition
files.Summary: A component that exists in the drawing but not in the design file — placed with the suite's own commands — to be written into the exported tab.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdComponentUpdate
files.Summary: One component's placement as it now stands in the drawing.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdCountGaps
files.Summary: What the drawing could not count for a tab, so that a count it gives may be low: parts whose 3D model is missing from the library (their collars are unseen) and parts the price list does not price (their cost is missing from the extra-hardware subtotal).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdDesign
files.Summary: A legacy design file parsed into a pure model.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdDesignTab
files.Summary: One design tab (structure) in a legacy design file.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdExportRefusedException
files.Summary: The export refused to write anything: a design height that is not a whole number of inches. The order system reads every DesignHeight as a whole number and, meeting one that is not, stops loading the whole file without a message - so a fractional height must never leave the suite.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdHardwareCounts
files.Summary: The hardware counts a design tab records for ordering. The order system prices exactly these numbers as written - it recounts none of them except an R3.5 collar count of zero - so they have to be true when the file leaves the suite.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdHeights
files.Summary: Design heights as the file must carry them: whole inches.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdLayerAudit
files.Summary:
Layer-vs-geometry disagreement report for an imported design file (ADR §4.4c's deferred import half). The legacy app cannot run this check on itself — a 2D canvas has no answer to "what stands on what" — so the designer's hand-typed tiers go unexamined until the texted top view splits into unreadable pages. The suite derives the storeys and can say where the file's own numbers contradict them.

This is a REPORT, never a correction: adoption of the file's numbering — including a privately inverted one — is the §4.4c rule, so the audit compares the PARTITION, not the labels. A walkable band wholly labeled 3 is consistent; a band split between two labels is not. On the reference corpus (11 files, 113 decks) the checks flag nothing, so a finding on a real file is signal, not noise.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdLayerAuditResult
files.Summary: What found in one design tab.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdLayerDisagreement
files.Summary: One place a design file's hand-typed Layer disagrees with its own geometry. Kind is a stable machine word for tests and grouping; Detail is the sentence a command prints.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdLayers
files.Summary:
Layer (storey/tier) assignment for components added to a design file (ADR §4.4c). The file's <Layer> integer is the legacy designer's hand-typed storey index — it filters the build in the Layer Manager and splits the texted top-view PDF into one page per tier. The legacy app cannot compute it (a 2D canvas has no answer to "what stands on what"), so designers maintain it by hand; the suite can, so additions derive their tier and an existing component's Layer is treated as designer evidence that is never rewritten and never "corrected".

Corpus-measured before writing (reference kcds, 9 multi-layer tabs, 128 deck placements): designer layers are clean non-interleaving height bands 9/9; the traversal tier below reproduces 102/128 hand assignments, and the misses are one file with privately inverted numbering (adoption keeps it) and tiers reached only by climbing links (adoption inherits them from the file's own bands). Height ALONE cannot draw the band line — the corpus holds a between-band gap equal to the largest within-band step (both 24") — which is why adjacency and footprint coincidence participate.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdLink
files.Summary: One owner→dependent pairing to write into a design file: a placed slide and the sit-down wall it carries. Reconciling a link writes BOTH directions — the owner's attachment slot (authoritative) and the dependent's back-reference — so the pair never lands in the one-way state reports.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdMatePoint
files.Summary: One mate point of a component in a legacy design file.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdNewFile
files.Summary:
New-design skeleton for F-035: a complete, empty legacy design file that can then pour components into — so a from-scratch drawing exports through the exact corpus-pinned writer the read-modify-write path uses, never a second component serializer.

The legacy app cannot be run here, so the envelope is deliberately a compatibility superset of the available evidence (the corpus and the legacy loader; citations in the source comments): the loader's hard requirements, the newest corpus writer's shape, both underlay forms, a complete production color scheme (an incomplete one opens but blocks saving in the legacy app), and the legacy writer's own empty-thumbnail fallback. Its hardware counts start at zero and are not left there: the order system prices them exactly as written, so the writer fills in each tab's real counts once its parts are in.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdNewPostSlot
files.Summary: A post slot of a component being added to a design file.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdPlacement
files.Summary: The design-canvas placement rule for legacy design files (F-029), verified against the demo/KCD corpus: slots on different components that share a PostID land on one world point under exactly this transform (sub-0.14" agreement; see KcdPlacementTests).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdPlanItem
files.Summary: One drawing component as the export's tab planner sees it.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdPostIds
files.Summary: Post-identity assignment for components added to a design file. A slot's PostID is the file's identity for a physical post: slots on different components sharing an id are one post, and the design's post count is the number of distinct ids. New slots therefore inherit the id of any post they land on and mint fresh ids otherwise.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdPostReconciliation
files.Summary: A design tab's post ids resolved against its own components. A slot's PostID has two meanings the legacy format never separates: most name a placed component (an insertable, surface-mount or Revolution post — the component IS the post), and the rest are abstract identities for posts that exist only as shared bookkeeping between deck corners. Counting the two as one number is what made real designs look wrong: a file whose every post is a placed component "declares" as many ids as it has post components, and comparing that against a geometric slot merge measures nothing. This record separates them so each part can be judged by the rule that actually applies to it.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.KcdWriter
files.Summary: Exporter for legacy design files (F-030): read-modify-write with preservation, the pattern the production web platform proved (KcdModel::updateProjectProperties). Only the slices the drawing owns are touched — component placements, deletions and additions in the tabs it writes, those tabs' hardware counts, and a design lock the edit invalidates; every other byte, including unknown or newer elements (Flag, MeshColors, POV), passes through opaquely. Not byte-exact by design, but components that didn't move keep their original text verbatim, and a tab whose content and counts did not change keeps all of its text.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.MateCandidateSet
files.Summary: The shared candidate-set primitive behind every mate-point consumer — the click path builds one per click, the F-032 jig builds one per jig start and queries it per cursor sample, and the F-033 osnap overrule shares for its per-entity variant. Precomputes every component's world-space mate points and a over the occupancy positions; adds a per-child grid over the compatible host points. The grids only narrow candidates: every returned match re-runs the exact per-host predicates of the original scan ( plus 's closed-interval distance rules), so answers are bit-identical to , the retained O(n²) oracle — the differential tests hold this to account.

Posts never occupy: they stand on corner slots, not mate points. Since Item 14 a post with known mating families () hosts a post-mounted child, one whose own list names Posts; a post without them hosts nothing, exactly as before.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.MateHarvest

Reads a component library's mate points straight off disk, so the plugin can use the library the designer actually has instead of only the table baked in at build time (build/build-mate-table.ps1 produces the same rows from the same files — MateHarvestEquivalenceTests holds the two to account).

This walks thousands of folders and must never run on a UI thread or inside an osnap/jig hot path (the F-033 rule); callers harvest once, off-thread, and swap the finished table in.

files.Summary: A component's plan footprint as an axis-aligned world box — what the stepping rule's "edge to edge" needs. A box is a conservative stand-in for a rotated or rounded part (it can only overstate the part's reach, never understate it), which is the safe direction for a report that must not invent findings.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PointGrid
files.Summary: A uniform 2D hash grid over indexed points — the O(1)-per-query replacement for "scan every point" proximity loops. Callers add points with their own indices and query for entries strictly within a tolerance, which is the coincidence predicate every ported legacy rule uses (see ). The grid only narrows the candidate set; every returned match re-checks the exact same comparison the O(n²) scans use, so results are bit-identical to a full scan — the differential tests in Playcraft.Core.Tests hold this to account.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PointSnapper
files.Summary: F-019 capture rule: the nearest declared mate point within a Euclidean radius of the pick wins; points that already have a child sitting on them are skipped in the nearest-search. The radius replicates the legacy engine; the occupancy skip is the suite's own addition — see the constants. Pure math — the plugin transforms points to world space and harvests occupied positions before calling in.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PostCaps
files.Summary: The legacy tool's cap rule (UpdatePostCap, PC2D:2860-2930, 7404-7466): a post gets a dome cap unless ANY owner's catalog PostCap is False. It is not "unless a roof covers it": most roofs are False but the TreeHouse roof is True, and toppers, the Butterfly extension and the stove pipe are False. Post Insertable posts always get one (PC2D:2916-2924); RV5 posts never. This only COUNTS caps; nothing here places them, and a designer's flat cap is decision #6's.

files.Summary: Which catalog families ARE posts — parts that stand a vertical structural post in their own right when placed as a component. Production designs are built this way: the 2026-08-04 corpus measurement found six of the seven harness design tabs resolve EVERY distinct PostID to a placed component in one of these families (the seventh, R507312CA, resolves four of six), so a component in a post family standing on a deck corner is that corner's post, and anything that counts or mints posts must treat it as one.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PostLength
files.Summary: The legacy tool's post length rule (GetRequiredPostHeight, PC2D:2932-3109): a post's length in whole feet is the largest any of its owners asks for. User decision 2026-10-02: the legacy tool's length is correct.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PostName
files.Summary: The one reader of post names. Post files and part numbers are dashed: S-1012-R35-0-103-144 (file), S-1012-R35-12ft (part), S-1008-R5F-9-048-087 (cut), P-1012-R35-0-103-144 (Post Insertable file), with -SM appended for surface mount. Every rule that needs a field of such a name asks here, so cut detection and lengths are read one way.

files.Summary: What a post's file or part name says about the post, read by .

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PostNumberFormatter
files.Summary: Post part numbers. A post's length is decided by the legacy tool's owner rule, (the tallest ask over every part standing on the post, in whole feet, surface mount 3 ft shorter); this class only spells the stock part that length names, zero-padded as the catalog files it: S-10{F:00}-{SYS}-{F:00}ft, with -SM for surface mount (). Factory-cut posts (S-1008-R5F-9-048-087) are a designer's manual tool, read by and never minted by the suite.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PostOwner
files.Summary: One owner of a post, as the rule sees it.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PostOwnerDiff
files.Summary: How a post's recorded owner list differs from the owners its position gives.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PostOwnerId
files.Summary: A post owner's identity in a drawing. A part placed directly in model space is its drawing handle, which persists in the DWG, so the owner lists the posts' XDATA records keep resolving. A part nested in a block is reached once per insert of that block, and every copy shares one reference handle (ComponentScan): the handle alone would give copies 2..N the first copy's posts, group and report lines. Its id is therefore the chain of enclosing insert handles, outermost first, then its own: one id per physical copy, stable while the inserts stand.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PostReconcileOptions
files.Summary: The policy a reconcile runs under: the inputs that decide what it may write, so the rules live in rather than in each caller's rewriting of its actions.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PostReconciler
files.Summary:
Diffs the drawing's posts against a plan. Matching is by position within the merge tolerance, so a kept post keeps its handle: this retires erase-and-remint for posts (ADR §4.2's deferred row, narrowed to fillers). Rules per matched post, the re-size policy among them:

  • held (nested, xref, locked layer): never written; reported when it disagrees;
  • a designer's cut post (): never touched, reported when it disagrees. The legacy tool re-sizes cut posts because its guard reads the wrong field; ours protects them (decision #11);
  • Post Insertable: re-sized upward only, reported when the plan wants it shorter, kept when its last owner goes (PC2D:3322-3331; DTF:15987). The new block keeps the P- file name while its part number is the standard S-10xx-…-xxft, as the legacy tool files them;
  • any other designer post (not the suite's own, not insertable): never re-sized, reported when it disagrees. It is the design's own component and quotes as one;
  • the suite's own posts, whatever their encoding: re-sized to the plan, both ways, except that a post one of whose owners has no post facts (the rule skipped it) is only lengthened, never shortened: the plan is then a floor, and the unread owner may need more.
An unmatched plugin post is deleted, unless it records an owner whose posts could not be read (); other unmatched posts are kept and reported (the suite never erases a designer's part). A planned post with no drawing post is added, or reported when refused. Under every re-size and removal is reported instead.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PostSlotOffsets
files.Summary: Item 14, instance height offsets: a design file saves each post slot's HeightOffset on the component that owns it, and the legacy tool lets that saved value override the library's (Component2D.cs:2386-2394). The tutorial's Bell Panel Pal is the case that needs it: the library says 0, TUTORIAL 2/5 says -2, and only the file's -2 sizes the store panel's far post to the legacy tool's 7 ft. This class pairs a file's slots with the library's, so the importer can store the offsets that differ and the exporter can write them back to the slot they came from.

files.Summary: A resolved stock post: its full catalog part number and its length.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PostSwing
files.Summary: Item 17, anchor and swing: a part held on a post by one end keeps that end put and swings round the post to follow the cursor, like a compass, settling on the directions the structure gives.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PriceBook
files.Summary: The offline price list: part number → MSRP/REP prices, loaded from the bundled CSV export of the company price workbook. Lookup is case-insensitive; duplicate part numbers keep the first row (the workbook lists one row per product NAME, so a part can appear several times at the same price).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PriceEntry
files.Summary: One price-book entry: a part with its retail (MSRP) and discounted (REP) price.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PricedBomBuilder
files.Summary: Applies prices to BOM lines and computes totals — the shared math behind the priced BOM command and the live BOM palette.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PricedBomResult
files.Summary: A fully priced BOM: rows plus totals.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.PricedRow
files.Summary: One priced BOM row. Unit prices are null when no source priced the part.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.ProductTypes
files.Summary: What kind of product a structure is, in the design file's own vocabulary (StructureProperties ProductType). The kind decides rules that differ between a play structure and everything else — extra hardware, for one, is a structure's alone.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.Pt
files.Summary: A 2D point in drawing inches. Deliberately free of AutoCAD types.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.QuoteSections
files.Summary: The reserved section names and the rules for what belongs in a section.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.Scene3DPlacement
files.Summary: The 2.5D→3D placement rule shared by the 3D view palette and any future 3D DWG export. World frame is AutoCAD's: X/Y the plan, Z up, inches. The library's 3D models anchor their ORIGIN on the component's mount plane (a deck's walking surface, an attachment's deck-edge mount, a post's base) — measured convention across the vault, validated by the collar math — so placement is a plain translate, never bounding-box re-anchoring.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.ScreenScale
files.Summary: Item 17: sizes the drag's words and markers in screen pixels, so they stay readable at any zoom. Drawn at a fixed 3 drawing units, the reason text was a few pixels tall at site zoom; the caller reads the live view each cursor sample and converts here.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.SectionKind
files.Summary: What KIND of thing a quote section is, which is what orders a quote. The kind is carried alongside the name rather than sniffed out of it: a section named "Site Amenities" could be a designer's group or a family roll-up, and only the code that resolved it knows which.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.SnapOutcome
files.Summary: Why did or didn't capture.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.SnapPoint
files.Summary: One mate point offered for capture, in world coordinates (the caller applies the host's block transform before choosing).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.SnapResult
files.Summary: The capture decision: the outcome and, when snapped, the point.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.StackCandidate
files.Summary: One placed deck as the stacking rule sees it: where its footprint stands, how far that footprint reaches from the insertion point, and which storey it belongs to.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.StackOutcome
files.Summary: Why did or didn't stack.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.StackResult
files.Summary: The stacking decision: the outcome, the deck it is about, and where the new deck goes.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.StructureCheck
files.Summary: What the drawing declares about its structures, checked against what the geometry shows. Pure comparison: it reports, it never reassigns.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.StructureGrouper
files.Summary: Which decks form one physical play structure, computed from the same shared-post adjacency PBGEN and PBFILL already use.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.StructureLines
files.Summary: One structure's own lines as the extra-hardware rule reads them: its placed components and its own counted hardware (collars, caps, deck-to-deck sets).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.SubItemExploder
files.Summary: Explodes a tallied BOM into its sub-components by walking the parent → child links in PartsSubItems. Pure: the caller supplies the row lookup, so the walk is unit-testable without a database and the Cad layer's only job is running one query per level.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.SubItemExplosion
files.Summary: An explosion pass: the sub-component lines plus what the pass could not trust. The notes exist because this data is hand-maintained — a silently dropped cycle or an unreadable quantity would turn into a short purchase list, so callers report them rather than presenting a clean total.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.SubItemLine
files.Summary: One exploded sub-component: a part the drawing needs because a top-level component contains it.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.SubItemRow
files.Summary: One PartsSubItems row as the explosion sees it. Every numeric column in that table is nvarchar, so the values arrive as raw text and are parsed here rather than at the database boundary — a price of "" or a quantity of "AR" is data the BOM has to survive, not an exception.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.SwingResult
files.Summary: A swing's answer: where the part stands and how it is turned.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.SwingSnap
files.Summary: What a swinging part's angle settled on.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.Transform2
files.Summary: The XY part of a placed block's transform (rotation / mirror / scale plus translation) — the bridge from mate-table coordinates, which are local to a part's insertion point, to world coordinates. Kept in Core so every consumer of mate positions (the click path, the F-032 jig, the F-033 osnap overrule) runs the identical transform math and can never disagree about where a mate point is.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.UnitPrices
files.Summary: Unit prices for one part: retail and (when known) discounted.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.UnmatchedMarker
files.Summary: A drawing marker no sidecar point sat on.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.UnmatchedSidecarPoint
files.Summary: A sidecar point no drawing marker sat on.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.VaultAttachmentPoint
files.Summary: A component attachment point: where a dependent part attaches.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.VaultComponent
files.Summary: A component parsed from a component-library 2D SVG. All coordinates are local to the component's insertion point with Y up (SVG is Y-down), in inches.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.VaultDescription
files.Summary: What a vault root turned out to contain, for reporting before trusting it.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.VaultFiles
files.Summary: The one way into the component library's files (Global Invariant 10: the library is read-only in every respect). Every path the suite builds into the library comes from here, and every read here opens the file for reading only, sharing it with anyone else. Nothing here, or anywhere else in src, opens a library file for writing; a source-discipline test holds that line.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.VaultFootingPoint
files.Summary: A component footing point: where it meets the ground and the footing it takes.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.VaultInventory
files.Summary: Inspects a component-library root without assuming which of the two known layouts it is: the development tree keeps the family folders under {root}\library with the data files at the root, while a designer pointing PBVAULT at their own library usually names the family-folder level directly (…\Access Components\S0-1291\…) with the data files at that level or one above. Everything here is inspection only — no caching, no AutoCAD — so the plugin can describe a path BEFORE committing to it.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.VaultMatePoint
files.Summary: A component mate point: where another component attaches and which way it faces.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.VaultPolyline
files.Summary: One connected polyline run: vertices with AutoCAD-style bulges (bulge[i] curves the segment from vertex i to i+1; tan(sweep/4)).

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.VaultSvgParser
files.Summary: Minimal parser for the component library's machine-generated SVGs. They use a constrained vocabulary: a JSON metadata block (insertion point, post slots, mate points) and path elements using only absolute M/L/A/Z commands. Anything outside that vocabulary throws — callers fall back to placeholder geometry rather than render a wrong shape.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.VaultXamlParser
files.Summary: Parser for the component library's native 2D geometry files — the legacy designer's own Component2D XAML ("{folder}.xaml"), the format the recovered library actually ships. It carries the same attachment metadata a design file's placed component does: the insertion point, the post slots (with their height offsets, and the Revolution slots some parts add), the mate points (with their length class and mate-type), the footing points, the attachment points, and the file's own part number, revision and design height — everything the library sidecar migrates from it. Produces the same contract as , so every downstream consumer (block build, filler pairing, mate snap) is source-agnostic.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.Xaml3DAssets
files.Summary: Filename preference for the library's exported 3D models ("{folder}-3D.xaml"). Pure string work so the tolerance rules are testable: the vault is hand-maintained and its known misnamings — a "-3D2" suffix, a "-3D_NEW" variant, two parts' files sharing one misfiled folder — must resolve to the right model instead of silently dropping the part.

files.Title: Playcraft.Core.Xaml3DMeshes
files.Summary: Minimal reader for the component library's exported 3D XAML models. It extracts collar mesh bounding boxes — the input to — by scanning MeshGeometry3D resources whose key starts with Collar_ (case-insensitive across the library's old COLLAR_ and current Collar_ conventions; CollarHW_ is hardware, not a collar, and never matches because of the underscore), and the R3.5 collars keyed KCR35_. Pure text parsing — no WPF — so it runs and tests headlessly.
